publicationStmt.p: Working ID register for the Digital Corpus of Armenian Colophons. Publication details and licensing will be established for the corpus.

sourceDesc.p: Colophon identities will be established from the project inventory, reviewed witnesses, and supporting scholarship. The first two entries are based on the working editions of col-000001 and col-000002.

projectDesc.p: This register defines the stable identity of each colophon as a textual record, independently of the physical witnesses preserving it. A record can be created before its edition is prepared. Each completed edition occupies one XML file named after the colophon identifier.

Witness records in witnesses.xml point to this register and to the manuscript or codicological unit preserving each occurrence. Witnesses are aggregated by their references to a colophon record; this register does not maintain a duplicate manual witness list.

editorialDecl.p: Colophon identifiers follow the pattern col-000001. Allocate each identifier once and retain it when the descriptive label, dating, attribution, or witness assessment changes.

Identification notes should state the scope of the textual record and any uncertainty about grouping occurrences as witnesses of one colophon. Shared wording or a similar formula alone does not establish textual identity. Witness grouping is a scholarly assessment and must remain evidence-based.

Add a ref of type edition only when its edition file exists. For example, the edition filename for col-000001 is col-000001.xml. Its relative directory will be agreed with the repository structure. The authority record and edition document are distinct resources and must be referenced explicitly.

Aim here is to keep the register concise. Transcriptions, translations, linguistic and formula annotations, detailed historical analysis, and witness comparisons belong in the edition. Witness loci and inscription dates belong to witness records; manuscript descriptions belong to manuscripts.xml.

revisionDesc.change: Added col-000001 and col-000002 to create basic template for review.

bibl.title: Colophon 1: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fols. 278v-280v 1099 CE (Armenian era 548), Alexandria
bibl.note: Colophon preserved in Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, recording the writing and completion of the Gospel in Alexandria in Armenian era 548 (1099 CE), with prayers for remembrance and a historical narrative.

Supply the corresponding entry in Matevosyan and Hovsepyan where available, including entry number and page references, with links to bibliography.xml. Record when no corresponding entry is available.

bibl.title: Colophon 2: Translation of the Martyrdom of Saints Eudoxios, Romylos, Zenon, and Makarios 1092 CE (Armenian era 541), Melitene
bibl.note: Translation colophon attached to the Martyrdom of Saints Eudoxios, Romylos, Zenon, and Makarios, recording translation from Greek into Armenian in Melitene in Armenian era 541 (1092 CE). It survives in the copies Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, MS. Arménien 178, Venice, Mekhitarist monastery of San Lazzaro MS. 17, and Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 6196. Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, MS. Arménien 178 is the earliest surviving copy in this example and the base witness; no original inscription of 1092 is preserved among these witnesses. The recorded translation date does not date the surviving copies.

Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 6196 also preserves a concluding prayer for Vardan, vardapet and recipient of the book. This prayer is retained within the same colophon record and distinguished from the shared translation colophon.
The relationship of the concluding Vardan prayer in Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 6196 to the earlier translation colophon remains open.

Supply the corresponding entry in Matevosyan and Hovsepyan where available, including entry number and page references, with links to bibliography.xml. Record when no corresponding entry is available.
